assumptions: Footnote 5's unqualified direction to confirm and demonstrate creates a minimum demonstration duty independently of a request.
Paragraph 14's request qualification continues to govern its broader or specifically requested demonstration; this reconciliation is uncertain.

citations.quote: Product Providers should confirm and, upon SFC’s request, demonstrate to the SFC’s satisfaction the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and the integrity of the smart contracts5.

5 Product Providers should confirm and demonstrate to the SFC that, at a minimum, they comply with the requirements as set out in paragraphs 10 to 13 above and the smart contracts are not subject to any contract vulnerabilities or security flaws with a high level of confidence.

Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain third party audit or verification on the management and operational soundness of the tokenisation arrangement, record keeping of ownership and integrity of the smart contracts.
Product Providers should, upon SFC’s request, obtain satisfactory legal opinion to support its application.

deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.distinction: On this rival reading, no request is needed for the footnote's minimum demonstration. Its strongest weakness is that it reduces the apparent effect of paragraph 14's express request qualification. Footnote 5 does not similarly remove the independent request conditions in paragraphs 15 and 16.

facts.meaning: The assessed actor and tokenisation arrangement fall within the Product Provider duties in paragraph 14 and footnote 5.

questions: Can the unqualified footnote impose a standing minimum demonstration while the main paragraph makes demonstration request-dependent?
Does paragraph 14's SFC satisfaction standard govern this standing minimum, and when must it be provided?
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] For an in-scope Product Provider, true means a minimum demonstration is called for under paragraph 14 and footnote 5 regardless of whether a request exists; false does not arise within this reading's scope. This is an obligation-activation predicate, not a finding of fulfillment. Footnote 5 independently requires confirmation and demonstration to the SFC of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and the specified smart-contract assurance. Read together with paragraph 14, SFC satisfaction plausibly governs the demonstration, while the reach of high confidence remains unresolved. Without a request, this minimum duty persists; paragraphs 15 and 16 do not activate their respective requirements to obtain third-party audit or verification and a satisfactory legal opinion.

The formalization selects activation of the minimum demonstration expectation, not its completion, due date or satisfactory performance.

deferred.481ce79be4fc0611266ee787.distinction: For a provider that has confirmed but has neither received a request nor demonstrated the minimum matters to the SFC, the preceding reading leaves demonstration untriggered; this reading treats minimum demonstration as independently expected. Absence of a stated deadline still prevents inferring that the provider is already overdue. The rival does not remove the separate request triggers in paragraphs 15–16.

questions: Is footnote 5 intended to create an independent demonstration expectation, and if so when must it be performed?
What remains of paragraph 14's request qualification under this reading: additional demonstration, its occasion or its manner? The packet does not settle this.
deferred.481ce79be4fc0611266ee787.statement: [TRUE_IS_SATISFIED] Within Product Provider scope, true means that the minimum demonstration expectation is activated without needing an SFC request; this proposed predicate is always true in scope and does not certify performance. Footnote 5 can be read as independently requiring confirmation and demonstration to the SFC of its stated minimum matters. Paragraph 14 retains the wider objects of soundness, ownership record keeping and integrity and its SFC satisfaction standard, but reconciling its request condition with this independent expectation remains the central uncertainty.

deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.unit_of_assessment: Activation of footnote 5's minimum demonstration duty for one Product Provider and tokenisation arrangement.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.temporal_basis: At assessment, while within scope; activation is unconditional on a request, but the excerpt supplies no performance deadline.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.true_means: Minimum demonstration of compliance with paragraphs 10–13 and the specified high-confidence smart-contract assurance is called for. This establishes neither performance nor SFC satisfaction. Reconciliation with paragraph 14's request condition and the reach of satisfaction and confidence remain unresolved. Paragraphs 15 and 16 retain their separate request conditions.
deferred.2249d844381920c4bb3ae2cf.false_means: False does not arise within scope under this reading. Being outside scope is not a finding of nonperformance.
